title: Unit and permutation invariance of supported Kummer products
statement:
Fix the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions], with arbitrary $n\geq1$, and the twists $A(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $X$ be any $k$-scheme and $c\geq0$. For an ordered tuple $h=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$ of global regular functions on $X$, let $C_h\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed subscheme locally defined by the ideal $(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, and put $D_a(h)=V(h_a)$ and $W_a(h)=X\setminus D_a(h)$. Using the concrete Kummer classes of [def-pur-frame-class], the localization boundaries of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], and the ordered supported cup product of [def-pur-supported-cup], write
$$K_X(h)=\mathop{\bigcup}_{a=1}^c\partial_{D_a(h)}\kappa_{W_a(h)}(h_a|_{W_a(h)})\in H^{2c}_{C_h}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A(c)),$$
where supported cohomology is [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The product is left-associated; at $c=0$ it is $1\in H^0(X,A)$ with $C_h=X$. This formula uses arbitrary functions, without smoothness, regularity, finite-type or separatedness hypotheses on $X$.

For every permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,c\}$ and every tuple of units $u_a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times$, set $h'_a=u_a h_{\sigma(a)}$. Then $C_{h'}=C_h$ as closed subschemes and
$$K_X(h')=K_X(h)\quad\text{in }H^{2c}_{C_h}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A(c)).$$
The equality uses the canonical identifications of support intersections and of $A(1)^{\otimes_A c}$ with $A(c)$; it requires no choice of a generator of the rank-one twist. In particular it applies to the frame classes of [def-pur-frame-class] after the canonical identification of both zero schemes with the same pullback support.

proof.text: The supports agree scheme-theoretically. On every affine open of $X$, multiplication of a generator by a unit does not change its principal ideal: $(u_a h_{\sigma(a)})=(h_{\sigma(a)})$, since the reverse inclusion follows by multiplying by $u_a^{-1}$. Reindexing a finite list does not change the sum of its principal ideals. Hence the two ideal sheaves, their closed subschemes, and their complementary opens coincide. The identifications of all intersections used below are those induced by these ideal equalities. If $c=0$, both supports are $X$ and both classes are the prescribed unit $1$, so the assertion holds. Assume $c>0$ below.

proof.text:
Fix one function $f$ and a global unit $u$ on $X$. Set $D=V(f)$ and $j:W=X\setminus D\hookrightarrow X$. The finite-level sheaf $A(1)$ is a finite-torsion coefficient sheaf, so the pro-etale localization exact sequence applies with no Cartier or smoothness hypothesis. Its consecutive arrows are
$$H^1(X,A(1))\xrightarrow{j^*}H^1(W,A(1))\xrightarrow{\partial_D}H^2_D(X,A(1)).$$
The Kummer pullback identity gives $\kappa_W(u|_W)=j^*\kappa_X(u)$. Exactness at the middle term therefore gives $\partial_D\kappa_W(u|_W)=0$. This uses a class already defined on $X$, not an assertion that a Kummer root of $u$ exists globally.

proof.text:
The functions $f$ and $uf$ have the same $D$ and $W$ by step 1. Both are units on $W$. Kummer additivity and the additivity of the localization boundary give
$$\begin{aligned}
\partial_D\kappa_W((uf)|_W)
 &=\partial_D\bigl(\kappa_W(u|_W)+\kappa_W(f|_W)\bigr)\\
 &=\partial_D\kappa_W(u|_W)+\partial_D\kappa_W(f|_W)
 =\partial_D\kappa_W(f|_W),
\end{aligned}$$
where the last equality is step 2. Thus multiplying any one defining function by a global unit leaves its degree-two supported boundary class unchanged. This calculation works for zero divisors and nilpotent functions as well as for regular functions.

proof.text:
Check the coefficient identification used in swapping factors. Write $L=A(1)_X$, a sheaf locally free of rank one in degree zero by clause (3) of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. By [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $A(r)=L^{\otimes_A r}$ for $r>0$. The symmetry $L\otimes_A L\to L\otimes_A L$ is the identity: locally choose a basis $e$ only to verify this morphism equality, and calculate
$$(ae)\otimes(be)=ab(e\otimes e)=ba(e\otimes e)=(be)\otimes(ae).$$
Tensor generators generate the sheaf tensor product, and equality of sheaf morphisms is local, so the identity holds globally and is independent of that temporary basis. Tensoring it with the identity on all remaining factors proves that an adjacent permutation acts trivially on $L^{\otimes_A c}=A(c)$ under the specified associativity identifications. This checks equality of coefficient morphisms locally; it does not try to detect global cohomology classes by restriction to a cover.

proof.text:
Put $\alpha_a=\partial_{D_a(h)}\kappa_{W_a(h)}(h_a|_{W_a(h)})$. To exchange two adjacent factors, associativity of supported cups rewrites the left-associated product as the product of its prefix, the block $\alpha_i\cup\alpha_{i+1}$, and its suffix; if either outside block is empty, simply omit it. The graded commutativity formula gives
$$\alpha_i\cup\alpha_{i+1}=(-1)^{2\cdot2}\alpha_{i+1}\cup\alpha_i=\alpha_{i+1}\cup\alpha_i.$$
The support symmetry is the canonical identification of the two intersections from step 1, and the coefficient symmetry contributes the identity by step 4. Substitution of this equality in the surrounding products and reassociation therefore leave the class in $H^{2c}_{C_h}(X,A(c))$ unchanged. Every input to graded commutativity is a degree-two class with coefficient $A(1)$, so the sign is $+1$ even when $\ell=2$.

proof.text: Any ordering of the finite list $1,\ldots,c$ can be put into the original order by moving the entry $1$ left to its first position through adjacent swaps, then moving the entry $2$ left within the remaining suffix, and continuing until the suffix is empty. At every move step 5 preserves the product, so $K_X(h_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,h_{\sigma(c)})=K_X(h)$. For each position $a$, step 3 identifies the boundary factor of $u_a h_{\sigma(a)}$ with the boundary factor of $h_{\sigma(a)}$. Substitute these $c$ equalities in the defining left-associated product, successively, to obtain $K_X(h')=K_X(h_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,h_{\sigma(c)})=K_X(h)$. The supports have already been identified as closed subschemes in step 1. Applied to a frame, the same ideal equality identifies its zero scheme with the given pullback support, so the final assertion follows too.
